name: The Well-League
summary: The hollowborn confederation: every settled oasis from the Glass Reach to the southern dunes, bound by water-law rather than borders. The Well-Sisters' councils govern locally; the League's one enforceable rule is the oldest — poison a well and answer to every well at once.

government.title: First Well-Sister (of the foremost oasis)
government.current: Well-Sister Mahal of the Deep Ring (Hollow Wells)
government.note: No central capital by design; Hollow Wells is 'foremost', not ruler. The League speaks through the Water-Moot, convened when any well is threatened.

population.note: northern factors; a permanent, uninvited Censer legation

laws: Water-law absolute: fouling a well is the League's single capital crime. Otherwise, oasis-councils rule locally and the code of the road governs caravans. No formal magic ban — discretion is the law of the sands.

relations.note: The cities dig where the League forbids; both need each other's trade.
The caravans are the League's hands and voice.

history_notes: Older than the Accords, the Edict, and most realms — the League dates itself to the first shared well.
Akhmat's Tears turned salty last month: the first salt-well in living memory, and the Water-Moot has been called.
adventure_hooks: Players attend the Water-Moot as neutral witnesses to the salt-well investigation.
A Censer legation demands the Relic Walk; the League offers players as 'impartial assessors' who must find grounds to refuse.
A Rememberers' cell in the Buried Gate is betrayed from inside; the League quietly asks players to find the traitor before the Censer does.
